findings.source_quote: ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται γῇ Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρας ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ τῷ τῆς ἀπειθείας τόπῳ ἐνδιατελεῖν
findings.english_quote: it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than to persist in the place of disobedience
findings.issue: The draft gives the comparison uneven grammatical scope: the first dative becomes the party for whom something is bearable, while the second becomes the location of an infinitive. The final ἐνδιατελεῖν can instead supply the subject of the impersonal comparison and govern both parallel locative datives. The existing note discusses only the second dative and does not disclose this materially different attachment. The English consequently leaves unclear what experiences are being compared.
findings.suggested_revision: A source-transparent candidate is: “it will be more bearable to remain in the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than in the place of disobedience.” Explain that this takes the final infinitive across both coordinated datives. Preserve the alternative attachment of γῇ to “bearable for” in a note, acknowledging the uneven comparison it produces rather than presenting the present mixed construction without explanation. The amended rendering requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ οὗτος ποικίλος, πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον κατὰ πάντα ἐξηλλαγμένος
findings.english_quote: and this multitude is diverse, each bird differing from another in every respect
findings.issue: The distributive interpretation is defensible, but “each bird” makes a referent choice that the note treats as settled. The masculine singular οὗτος and ἐξηλλαγμένος grammatically refer to ὄχλος; τὸν ἕτερον can therefore be understood as another multitude or group, rather than necessarily another individual bird. This affects whether the stated differences concern individuals or groups/kinds.
findings.suggested_revision: If retaining “each bird,” expand the source-quoted note to acknowledge the collective agreement and the alternative comparison between groups or kinds of birds. Explain that the individualizing reading is chosen contextually because the following catalogue describes distinguishing features. Alternatively, consider “and this multitude is diverse, one differing from another in every respect,” with a note preserving the unresolved referent. This is a disclosure revision, not an unresolved-source block.
